lines.en: Excuse me! **What time does** English class **start**?
lines.pt: Com licença! A que horas começa a aula de inglês?
É da manhã ou da tarde/noite?

lines.en: Great. And **when is** the speaking test?
lines.pt: Ótimo. E quando é a prova de fala?

lines.en: It’s next Friday at two p.m.
lines.pt: É na próxima sexta, às duas da tarde.

lines.en: No, on Friday. There’s no class on Monday.
lines.pt: Não, na sexta. Não há aula na segunda.
A que horas a aula termina?

lines.en: At eleven. Have a good day!
lines.pt: Às onze. Tenha um bom dia!

pages.title: Asking about the schedule

situation.text: You are a new student at a language school in the United States. You ask the front desk when class starts, when the test is and which day it is.

pages.goal: By the end of the class you can ask what time something starts or ends, ask when an event is, check the day and understand a.m. and p.m.
canDo: Ask the time: What time does… start?
Ask the day: When is…? / Is it on Monday?
Check the time: Is that a.m. or p.m.?
Understand days and times in a short answer
success: I repeat the information to be sure.
pages.think: In Brazil you say “às 14h”. How do you think people say this in the United States?

teach.goal: Abrir pela situação real: não perder a aula nem a prova por não entender o horário.
solo: Pergunte se o estudante já perdeu um compromisso por confundir horário ou dia.
Mostre os 4 critérios de sucesso.
group: Cada estudante diz um horário em português; o grupo tenta dizer em inglês.
Mostre os critérios: serão a missão final.
extra: What time do you wake up?
Which day is your favorite?
support: Aceite respostas em português e reformule em inglês.

pages.title: Connection & warm-up

intro.solo: Start with real questions about the student’s week.
intro.group: One question per student, then a question back to a classmate.

pages.recall: First day in class (last lesson): “How do you spell…?”. Ask: How do you spell your last name?

qs.pt: Qual é o seu dia mais cheio?

pages.tip: Use the answers to find gaps with numbers and days.

teach.goal: Entrar no idioma e testar números e dias da semana.
extra: What time do you eat lunch?
What do you do on Sundays?
support: Mostre os chips de resposta e peça que escolham.

pages.title: Cultural snapshot — Life in the USA
pages.intro: Times and schedules look different in the United States. Look at the cards and guess before you read.

cards.note: Daily life: 9:30 a.m., 2:00 p.m. — a.m. is morning, p.m. is afternoon and night.
Many colleges use Mon/Wed/Fri or Tue/Thu classes.
In the US it is used mainly by the military and some jobs, like hospitals.

levels.A2: They say “two p.m.” or “two in the afternoon”.
levels.B1: They use the 12-hour clock: 2 p.m. instead of 14:00.
levels.B2: In daily life they use a.m./p.m. and avoid 14:00, except in the military or some professions.

qs.q: Why is a.m. or p.m. important?
qs.pt: Por que a.m. ou p.m. é importante?

levels.A1: 9 a.m. is morning. 9 p.m. is night.
levels.A2: Without it, “nine” can be morning or night.
levels.B1: Because the same number appears twice a day, so you must be clear.
levels.B2: Without a.m./p.m. the time is ambiguous, so people often add “in the morning” or “at night”.

qs.q: How can you be sure about a time?

levels.A2: I say: “Is that a.m. or p.m.?”
levels.B1: I repeat the time and ask them to confirm.
levels.B2: I repeat it, check the day and ask them to write it down if it is important.

pages.compare: In Brazil many schedules and tickets use the 24-hour clock (14h, 18h30). In the US it is usually a.m./p.m. What do you use at school or work?

teach.goal: Ativar o contexto do relógio de 12 horas e das grades de horários.
solo: Mostre os cartões e peça hipóteses.
Escreva 14:00 e peça que diga “two p.m.”.
group: Cada estudante escolhe um cartão e explica.
Pergunte “Do you agree?”.
answers: Q2: the same number appears morning and night.
Q3: Is that a.m. or p.m.?
extra: What time do your classes or work start?
Do you like the 24-hour clock?
support: Use as respostas A1 como andaime.
stretch: B2: compare grades de horário em escolas do Brasil e dos EUA.

pass1.pt: Sobre o que a Alma pergunta?

teach.goal: Compreender horários e dias antes de ver o texto.
solo: Esconda o texto. 1ª escuta: tema.
2ª escuta: hora de início, dia da prova, hora da prova, término.
group: Duplas anotam antes de revelar.
Compare as respostas.
answers: Pass 2: nine thirty · Friday · two (p.m.) · eleven
extra: Is the class in the morning or afternoon?
Why does Alma ask “a.m. or p.m.?”
support: Use “Slow” na 2ª escuta e pause depois de cada informação.

qs.q: What time does the class start?

retell.prompt: Retell the conversation in your own words, at your level.

teach.goal: Ler o diálogo, perceber os chunks e recontar.
solo: Papéis invertidos na 2ª leitura.
Peça que reconte.
group: Leitura em duplas e troca de papéis.
Reconto em cadeia.
answers: 9:30 a.m. · next Friday · no · at eleven
extra: What time is the test? (two p.m.)
What day is it today?

errors.r: What time does the class start?

support: Mostre o PT depois da 2ª leitura.

pages.title: Useful expressions

items.use: Ask the start time of a class, a movie, a meeting.
Ask the day or date of an event.
Check the day. Use “on” with days.

items.pt: É da manhã ou da tarde/noite?
items.use: Make sure you have the right part of the day.
Give a start time: It starts at nine.
Ask for the time in writing when it is important.

pages.note: Choose 3–5 expressions (★) to use again and again.

teach.goal: Escolher 3–5 chunks e descobrir a função de cada um.
solo: Pergunte “When do you say it?”.
Peça um exemplo com a rotina do estudante.
group: Cada estudante escolhe uma ★ e explica.
Compare em duplas.
answers: Asking the time · Asking the day · Checking · Answering · Asking for help
extra: Which one do you need for your own schedule?

patterns.name: Asking for a time
ex: What time does the test end?
What time does the library close?

head: Spoken English
Written English
rows: At what time does the session begin?
Will it take place on Monday?
register.note: These are differences of context and register, not absolute rules.

teach.goal: Fixar 2 padrões (What time does… / When is…?); on para dias, at para horas.
solo: Mostre o padrão no diálogo.
Use “Swap the words”.
group: Troca em cadeia.
Em pares: um escolhe as peças.
teach.answers: Padrões 01/02 são o foco; 03/04 são expansão.
extra: Change the day and say the sentence.
Ask the same question about your job.

errors.r: What time does the class start?

support: Só What time does… start? na primeira rodada.
stretch: Combine: When is the test, and what time does it start?

pages.title: Pronunciation lab — natural American English
pages.tip: Thirteen has the strong sound at the end (thir-TEEN). Thirty has it at the start (THIR-ty). That changes the time!

own.prompt: Say three times you know: your class start, your lunch and your bedtime.
own.criteria: Did your partner understand 13 vs 30 and 15 vs 50?

teach.goal: UM só fenômeno: acento nos números -teen × -ty.
solo: Modele thirteen × thirty e peça que o estudante bata na sílaba forte.
Faça o identify e depois o uso próprio.
group: Coro, depois duplas: um diz, o outro identifica.
Cada um cria uma hora própria.
support: Use gestos: mão alta para a sílaba forte.

levels.h: Controlled practice — choose the best answer

items.q: 1. You want the start time of class.
2. You want the date of the test.
items.why: When is…? asks for the day or date.

items.q: 3. You hear “nine”. You are not sure.
4. The class is on Friday. Which is correct?

levels.h: Guided practice — complete, substitute and transform

items.q: You want to be sure. Choose the best reply.
items.why: Check the part of the day.

teach.goal: Do controlado ao guiado antes da fala livre.
solo: Peça que justifique cada resposta.
Se acertar rápido, peça a pergunta mais polida.
group: Resolvam em duplas e comparem.
Equipes: ponto por resposta justificada.
answers: 1: What time does class start? · 2: When is the test? · 3: Is that a.m. or p.m.? · 4: It’s on Friday.
Gap: does · on · When is the speaking test? · Is it on Monday? · Is that a.m. or p.m.? · Thanks! Eleven a.m.?
extra: Say each answer with the time you really have class.
support: Ofereça o banco de palavras nas lacunas.

pages.title: Personalized roleplay — check your schedule

brief.teacher: You are the front desk. Give times and days quickly, and change one detail during the scene.
brief.student: You are a student: find out the time, the day and a.m./p.m. for your class and test.

orders: Ask the start time of the class
Ask the day of the speaking test
complications: The desk says a time too fast.
The class changes to another day.
You do not know if it is a.m. or p.m.
The desk says thirteen but you heard thirty.

teach.goal: Simulação com complicação e três rodadas com menos apoio.
solo: Use o horário real das aulas do estudante.
Rodada 1: chunks. Rodada 2: palavras-chave. Rodada 3: sem roteiro.
Anote 2–3 correções.
extra: What if the class changes to another day?

errors.w: The class is on the 2 hours.
errors.r: The class is at two o’clock.

stretch: Remarque a prova e confirme a nova data.

pages.title: Group mission — plan the week
pages.goal: Each group must find the right time and day, check it and confirm it.

missions.mission: Find out when and at what time the English class and the test are.
You both want the same class. Check the days and the a.m./p.m. and choose one.
missions.constraint: Use “Is it on…?” and “Is that a.m. or p.m.?”

missions.mission: The teacher changes the class day. Ask for the new day and the time and write it down.
missions.constraint: Ask “Could you write it down?” once.

teach.goal: Realizar algo com o inglês: resolver o horário.
group: Cada grupo recebe papel, restrição e missão.
Progressão: com apoio → palavras-chave → sem roteiro.
Anote 2–3 correções.
answers: Modelo: “What time does the class start?” → “At nine thirty.” → “Is that a.m. or p.m.?” → “A.m.”
extra: What if the teacher changes the day again?
support: Dê o início de frase em cada cartão.

pages.title: Writing — a small real-life task
pages.task: Write a short message to a friend with your class schedule for next week. Give two days and two times.
pages.model: Hi Sam! My class is **on Monday** and Wednesday. **It starts at** 9:30 a.m. and ends at 11:00 a.m. The test is on Friday at 2:00 p.m. See you soon!
checklist: I used on with the days.
pages.tip: Fix only 2–3 priority points. Show a more natural way to say the same idea.

teach.goal: Produção escrita curta ligada à situação.
solo: Peça o texto; corrija 2–3 pontos.
group: Troquem os textos e corrijam em duplas.
extra: Add the room number.
support: Dê o modelo e peça só para trocar dias e horas.

criteria.name: Fluency
criteria.desc: Mantém a comunicação sem interrupções excessivas.

criteria.name: Language use
criteria.desc: Utiliza adequadamente padrões, vocabulário e expressões.

criteria.name: Pronunciation
criteria.desc: É compreensível e usa ritmo e entonação adequados.

criteria.name: Interaction
criteria.desc: Responde, pergunta, esclarece e desenvolve a conversa.

interpret.text: Needs more support. Revisit the main patterns with guided practice before the next lesson.
Functional performance. Work on the lowest criteria in the next lesson.
Good control. Raise complexity and speed; add follow-up questions.
Strong performance. Move to a more demanding situation.

prompts.well: Example: You asked about the day and checked a.m. or p.m.
prompts.next: Example: Ask for two schedule changes without notes.

teach.goal: Avaliar o que o aluno conseguiu comunicar, não só os erros gramaticais.
solo: O estudante se autoavalia primeiro; depois você.
Feche com os três blocos: What you did well · What to improve · Your next challenge.
group: Dê um comentário por critério a cada estudante.
Cada um escolhe o próprio próximo desafio.
teach.answers: A rubrica é uma ferramenta interna de acompanhamento, não uma certificação CEFR.

pages.title: Level up — the same situation from A1 to C2
pages.intro: You do not need six different methods: the structure stays, while language complexity and autonomy grow.

ladder.say: What time does the class start? Is it on Monday?
ladder.goal: Ask about the time and day.

ladder.say: Could you tell me what time the speaking test starts on Friday?
I was wondering whether the schedule has changed, since the class used to start earlier.
I’d appreciate it if you could confirm whether the session has been moved to the afternoon.
Might I trouble you to confirm whether the revised timetable still holds for Friday’s session?

pages.note: This progression is illustrative: complex sentences do not define a level on their own. CEFR also considers comprehension, autonomy, fluency, accuracy, interaction and appropriateness.

teach.goal: Mostrar a progressão sem criar seis metodologias.
solo: Mostre onde o estudante está e a próxima etapa.
group: Cada um escolhe a frase do próprio nível e a do próximo.
